<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">DECEMBER 31, 2010 AND 2009</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company leased office space for its New York, New York location (the &#8220;1<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">st</font> NYC Office&#8221;), under a five-year lease agreement bearing monthly rent of $8,798.&#160;&#160;In September 2008, the Company relocated to a larger space in New York (the &#8220;2<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">nd</font> NYC Office&#8221;), where the Company entered into a six-year lease agreement bearing monthly rent of $25,073 with an annual 2.5% escalation.&#160;&#160;In March 2009, the Company subleased the 1<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">st</font> NYC Office space for the remainder of the original lease term with rent commencing June 1, 2009 at a monthly rate of $6,986 with an annual 2.5% escalation at the beginning of each calendar year.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Company has recognized in accrued expenses an early cease use liability of $23,500 pertaining to 1<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">st</font> NYC Office space.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On March 11, 2010, the Company entered into a lease agreement to relocate its New York City headquarters to a larger space (the &#8220;3<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">rd</font> NYC Office&#8221;), having 16,840 square feet.&#160;&#160;The lease term for the 3<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">rd</font> NYC Office is 92 months commencing on May 1, 2010, bearing monthly rent of $49,117 with an annual 2.5% escalation.&#160;&#160;In connection with the 3<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">rd</font> NYC Office lease agreement, a banking institution issued an irrevocable 1-year standby letter of credit for the benefit of the landlord.&#160;&#160;The Company opened a certificate of deposit with the banking institution in the amount of $294,700 and pledged that to the letter of credit.&#160;&#160;Through the lease term of the 3<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">rd</font> NYC Office, the Company is required to maintain a standby letter of credit for the benefit of the landlord. Accordingly, as of December 31, 2010, the Company has classified the certificate of deposit, including accrued interest, as restricted cash, a non-current asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company entered into an agreement to sublease the office space of the 2<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">nd</font> NYC Office commencing May 1, 2010 for the remainder of the original lease term with monthly rent of $16,717 with an annual 2.5% escalation.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the Company recognized an early cease use liability of $497,851 pertaining to the 2<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">nd</font> NYC Office space.&#160;&#160;The charge to operations for the establishment of the liability was partially offset by $66,350 due to the elimination of deferred rent related to the 2<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">nd</font> NYC Office space.&#160;&#160;The balance of the early cease use liability was $384,771 at September 30, 2010, of which $306,578 is long-term.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 22, 2010, the Company entered into a 5-year agreement, commencing June 1, 2010, for office space in Santa Monica, California bearing monthly rent of $3,827 with an annual 3.0% escalation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In October 2008, the Company leased office space in San Francisco, California under a month-to-month lease agreement bearing monthly rent of $3,371.&#160;&#160;Commencing August 1, 2009, the Company relocated this office to another space in San Francisco, where the Company entered into a five-year lease agreement bearing monthly rent of $3,089.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In December 2008, the Company leased office space from a sub-landlord in Chicago, Illinois under a 6-month agreement bearing monthly rent of $1,400 commencing January 1, 2009.&#160;&#160;Commencing July 1, 2009, this lease agreement was renewed for one year bearing monthly rent of $1,400.&#160;&#160;Effective February 1, 2010, the Company entered into a 16-month lease directly with the landlord bearing a monthly payment of $2,151, increasing to $2,216 on June 1, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Separation Agreement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 1, 2010, the Company entered into a Separation Agreement (the &#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with Michael Mathews (CEO of the Company at that time) who will resign from the Company following a transition period. Under the terms of the Agreement, effective January 31, 2011, Mr. Mathews&#8217; employment agreement will be terminated and he will no longer serve as the Chief Executive Officer of the Company.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the Agreement, Mr. Mathews will receive a payment of $177,500 which is equal to six months of his current annual base salary. As of December 31, 2010 this payment was included in accrued expenses in the consolidated balance sheet.&#160;&#160;The Company also agreed to continue to provide Mr. Mathews his existing medical and dental coverage through the end of 2011, after which time Mr. Mathews will be eligible for benefit continuation under COBRA. In addition, the Company agreed that, if the Company achieves its 2010 annual milestones, and the board approves bonus payments to executive officers, the Company will pay to Mr. Mathews his second half 2010 bonus of $88,750. Such milestones were achieved and the second half of Mr. Mathews&#8217; bonus was included in accrued expenses in the consolidated balances sheet as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Both the Company and Mr. Mathews agreed to mutual releases, subject to certain exceptions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Legal Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">From time to time, the Company may be involved in litigation relating to claims arising out of the Company&#8217;s operations in the normal course of business.&#160;&#160;Except for the following,&#160;the Company is not currently a party to any material litigation.&#160;&#160;On or about December 8, 2010, Sonal Bose commenced an action in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Sonal Bose v. Interclick, Inc.</font>, Case No. 10 Civ. 9183-DAB (S.D.N.Y.)) alleging that interclick engaged in certain activities that&#160;&#160;plaintiff claims violate electronic privacy and computer use laws. The plaintiff&#160;&#160;asserts federal and state law claims, and&#160;&#160;seeks compensatory, statutory, and punitive damages, restitution, and reimbursement of expenses and attorneys&#8217; fees.&#160;&#160;The plaintiff also seeks injunctive and declaratory relief and class action certification.</font><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On or about December 23, 2010, Sonal Bose commenced a&#160;&#160;related&#160;&#160;action in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York against McDonald&#8217;s Corporation, CBS Corporation, Mazda Motor of America, Inc., and Microsoft Corporation (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Sonal Bose</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">v. McDonald&#8217;s Corporation; CBS Corporation; Mazda Motor of America, Inc.; and Microsoft Corporation</font>, Case No. 10 Civ. 9569-DAB&#160;&#160;(S.D.N.Y.)) alleging that the actions of interclick caused the defendants to violate various laws&#160;&#160;and&#160;&#160;seeking class action certification.&#160;&#160;The Company is not a party to this action but are providing for the defense of the case at our expense based upon indemnification obligations in our standard agency agreements.&#160;&#160;The complaint asserts the same&#160;&#160;claims as are alleged in the complaint against interclick, together with a cause of action for tortious interference, and seeks similar relief.</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 28, 2011, motions to dismiss each of the foregoing cases were filed, which are pending.&#160;&#160;As noted in the motions to dismiss, interclick believes the cases are entirely without merit and interclick intends to vigorously defend its prior practices and technology.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has a 401(k) Savings Plan (the &#8220;401(k) Plan&#8221;) that qualifies as a deferred salary arrangement under Section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code. Under the 401(k) Plan, participating employees may elect to contribute up to 100% of their eligible compensation, subject to certain limitations. The 401(k) Plan provides for a discretionary employer matching contribution.&#160;&#160;&#160;The Company made no matching contribution to the 401(k) Plan in 2010 or 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">DECEMBER 31, 2010 AND 2009</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 14. Concentrations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Concentration of Credit Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentration of credit risk consist of cash and cash equivalents and accounts receivable.&#160;&#160;Cash and cash equivalents are deposited in three financial institutions.&#160;&#160;The balance, at any given time, may exceed Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insurance limits.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010 and 2009, there was approximately $14,521,000 and $13,336,000, respectively, in excess of FDIC insurable limits.</font></div>
